objective: Declare every intended Gold explanatory variable, the candidate reaction horizons, and the prior-context fields, so individual-variable coverage can be audited deterministically before combination research. This file declares scope and mappings; it contains no measurements and no success claims.

declared_inventory_source.derivation: Ten weighted Layer 1 factors (F1-F10) plus explicit event decomposition. Twenty of the twenty-eight entries are levels or transformations of five macro/price series; they are not twenty independent raw inputs.
declared_inventory_source.original_research_document_gap: The originally supplied external research documents were not available in this checkout. Coverage below is verified against the repository logic document and local versioned sources only.

fact_classes.verified: Observed directly in a named local file, module constant or checked-in document during this milestone.
fact_classes.proposed: A mapping or transformation declared as intended but not yet demonstrated against a source.
fact_classes.unavailable: Required by the declared inventory but no local source and no verified mapping exists. Retained explicitly rather than dropped.

horizons.label: Immediate event window (sub-hourly)
horizons.notes: Hourly candles cannot establish a minute-level reaction. No minute-level reaction is claimed or inferred from H1 bars; the offset stays undeclared.

horizons.label: One hour after anchor
horizons.notes: Most US releases occur at 13:30Z or 15:00Z, which are not H1 candle boundaries. The anchor-to-candle alignment rule, and whether partial bars are admitted, must be declared before measurement.

horizons.label: Four hours after anchor
horizons.notes: Endpoints can fall inside session closures. Continuity of the four intervening hourly bars is reported separately from endpoint existence.

horizons.label: Twenty-four elapsed hours after anchor
horizons.notes: Preserves the existing exact-24-hour contract. This milestone does not modify the strict 24-hour evaluator; the audit reads endpoint and continuity availability only.

horizons.label: Five trading days after anchor
horizons.local_source_resolution: H1 bars aggregated to a declared session close
horizons.notes: Five trading days is explicitly NOT 120 elapsed hours. A declared XAU/USD session open/close, holiday list, early-close rule and rollover handling are required before this horizon is measured.

prior_context.definition: Return of the Gold mid price from the session close five trading days before the observation to the last observation strictly before it.
prior_context.leakage_guard: The window ends before the observation begins and never includes the observation's own outcome window.

prior_context.definition: Realized volatility of Gold H1 mid-price returns over the trailing five trading days. Estimator (simple vs log returns), sampling window and annualisation must be declared before use.
prior_context.leakage_guard: Uses completed bars only; the bar containing the observation is excluded.

prior_context.definition: Change in basis points between the real-yield observations at index -1 and -6 in observation order, strictly before the cutoff. This is an observation-index lookback and is not a claim about five calendar trading days.
prior_context.leakage_guard: A vintage becomes available at realtime_start plus the declared conservative lag; the vintage date and the observation date must both precede the cutoff.

prior_context.definition: Change in basis points between the two-year yield observations at index -1 and -6 strictly before the cutoff, on the same observation-index basis.
prior_context.leakage_guard: Same vintage-availability guard as the real-yield lookback.

prior_context.definition: Change in basis points between the nominal 10-year yield observations at index -1 and -6 strictly before the cutoff. The series exists in local vintages but is not one of the declared 28 variables.
prior_context.leakage_guard: Same vintage-availability guard as the real-yield lookback.

prior_context.definition: Percentage change between the broad trade-weighted US dollar index observations at index -1 and -6 strictly before the cutoff.
prior_context.leakage_guard: Same vintage-availability guard as the yield lookbacks.
prior_context.caveat: DTWEXBGS is a broad trade-weighted index, not ICE DXY. It must not be relabelled as the declared dxy_* variables.

prior_context.definition: Sign, event family and relative size of the most recent US release strictly before the cutoff. Surprise differences are comparable only inside one event family; they are not a cross-family numeric score.
prior_context.leakage_guard: Uses the release timestamp and the archive lastUpdated vintage. Archived consensus values are not authenticated pre-release vintages, so this field stays retrospective.

prior_context.definition: Elapsed hours between the release timestamp of the most recent US release strictly before the cutoff and the cutoff itself.
prior_context.leakage_guard: Only releases with a release timestamp strictly before the cutoff can be selected.

forbidden_context.reason: The eventual direction of the observation's own horizon is the label, not context. Conditioning on it leaks the outcome and is prohibited.
A value whose realtime_start or lastUpdated falls after the cutoff is a revision, not information available at observation time.
Any price used for context must come from strictly before the observation anchor; the observation's own reaction window is never context.

variables.label: US 10-year real yield
variables.definition: 10-year constant-maturity real yield level (FRED DFII10).

source_mapping.record_shape: observations[] with { date, realtime_start, realtime_end, value }

timestamp_semantics.availability: realtime_start plus the conservative 36-hour lag used by backtester/lib/gold_macro_vintage_dataset.js

known_gaps: Authenticated release time unavailable.

variables.label: US 10-year real yield five-observation change
variables.definition: Change in the 10-year real yield level, in basis points, between the current observation and the observation five positions earlier.

source_mapping.rule: 100 * (level_t - level_t-5) on FRED daily observations in observation order

timestamp_semantics.availability: the later of the two source vintages plus the conservative 36-hour lag

variables.label: Gold spot price
variables.definition: XAU/USD spot price level used for outcome measurement and for price context.

source_mapping.record_shape: candles[] with { time, complete, volume, bid{o,h,l,c}, mid{o,h,l,c}, ask{o,h,l,c} }

timestamp_semantics.availability: H1 bar open time; a bar is only complete at open time plus one hour
timestamp_semantics.note: Bar time is the nominal hourly boundary. Partial session bars and closures are not classified by the source.

known_gaps: No declared trading-session calendar, so session boundaries and early closes are unresolved.
The immediate sub-hourly window is not measurable at H1 resolution.
Candle completeness is a source flag only; it does not certify continuous trading.

variables.label: Gold one-day percentage change
variables.definition: Percentage change of the Gold price over the preceding one trading day.

source_mapping.rule: percentage change between the current session close and the previous session close, on a declared session calendar
source_mapping.note: No local module derives this from the Gold H1 archive. The name appears only as an input field in the live agent, the replay cores and asset-builder outputs, so the research mapping is proposed, not verified.

timestamp_semantics.availability: pending session calendar

known_gaps: No local derivation exists; the session close and calendar are undeclared.
Stored production snapshots show the live pipeline falling back to this field when gold_d5_pct is missing, so the same name can carry different lookbacks.

source_mapping.rule: percentage change between the current session close and the close five trading days earlier, on a declared session calendar
source_mapping.note: Proposed. Five trading days is not 120 elapsed hours and no session calendar is declared yet.

timestamp_semantics.availability: pending session calendar

known_gaps: No local derivation exists.

Observed in production to be absent, with the live pipeline substituting the one-day change.

variables.label: US economic event family
variables.definition: Identity of the released US economic indicator, used both as the event anchor and as the family label for surprise comparisons.

source_mapping.record_shape: array of { id, eventId, name, dateUtc, periodDateUtc, periodType, countryCode, currencyCode, unit, volatility, potency, actual, revised, consensus, previous, ratioDeviation, isBetterThanExpected, lastUpdated, ... }
source_mapping.observed_scope: This local merged archive contains only countryCode=US rows.

timestamp_semantics.availability: the archive exposes a lastUpdated epoch field, but its meaning is archive-update time, not authenticated original publication time

known_gaps: Family identity is stable, but releases repeat and one daily observation can span several families.
No mapping exists between archive family names and the live agent's latest_us_event vocabulary.
Higher unemployment is not the same economic signal as higher payrolls; direction conventions must stay family-specific.

variables.label: Released value of the event
variables.definition: Reported actual value of the release as stored in the archive.

timestamp_semantics.availability: present at release; the archive value is the current archived value, not a proven original release print

known_gaps: Null actuals occur for unpublished, tentative, preliminary or speech rows and must not be coerced to zero.
Units differ per family, so cross-family numeric comparison is invalid.

variables.label: Pre-release consensus for the event
variables.definition: Consensus expectation stored alongside the release.

timestamp_semantics.observation_time: intended to be the pre-release consensus
timestamp_semantics.availability: unverified. The archive stores a single consensus value with no vintage; it may be a revised or post-release figure.
timestamp_semantics.note: This is the central provenance gap for event research: without an authenticated pre-release vintage an actual-versus-consensus surprise is retrospective evidence.

known_gaps: No consensus vintage.
Nulls exist and are a genuine missing state.
Consensus for preliminary rows can refer to different period definitions.

variables.label: Previous value as originally released
variables.definition: The prior period value as it stood at that prior release, before any restatement.

source_mapping.rule: the actual value recorded for the same event family at its preceding release
source_mapping.note: The archive exposes a `previous` field and a `previousIsPreliminary` flag, but no as-released history. The archived previous value may already include a restatement, so it must not be used as the original print.

timestamp_semantics.availability: retrospective only; the archived previous value carries no vintage

known_gaps: No as-released previous-value history.
Restatements are indistinguishable from original prints.
Requires the per-family release sequence to be built deterministically.

variables.label: Event surprise direction and family-relative size
variables.definition: Sign and, within one event family, magnitude of the difference between the release actual and the consensus.

source_mapping.rule: direction is actual > consensus, actual = consensus or actual < consensus; a numeric difference is comparable only within the same family and unit
source_mapping.also_available: the archive carries ratioDeviation and isBetterThanExpected, but neither formula or scaling is declared in this repository

timestamp_semantics.availability: inherits the unverified consensus vintage, so the surprise is retrospective only

known_gaps: Direction is well defined; comparable magnitude is not, because units differ per family.
ratioDeviation and isBetterThanExpected are stored but undocumented, so they are not admissible as a cross-family score.
The live agent's rule treats a positive surprise as bearish for Gold, which is a hypothesis to test rather than an established relationship.

variables.label: Hours since the event release
variables.definition: Elapsed hours between the release timestamp and the observation anchor.

source_mapping.rule: anchor time minus dateUtc, in hours

timestamp_semantics.availability: non-negative by construction; a negative value means the anchor preceded the release and must be rejected

known_gaps: Releases repeat per family, so age alone does not identify which release is being measured.
Rows with null or unparsable dateUtc must be excluded rather than assigned an age.

timestamp_semantics.availability: realtime_start plus the conservative 36-hour lag

known_gaps: Not part of the declared inventory, so any use must be declared explicitly rather than folded into an existing variable.

additional_local_series.label: Broad trade-weighted US dollar index
additional_local_series.definition: FRED DTWEXBGS broad trade-weighted US dollar index level. Present locally and previously used as a dollar proxy.

timestamp_semantics.availability: realtime_start plus the conservative 36-hour lag

known_gaps: This is not ICE DXY and must not be reported as the declared dxy_* variables.
Its publication is weekly-weighted with longer revisions, so the fixed 36-hour lag is a weaker assumption here than for the daily yield series.

derived_name_aliases.note: The local macro engine emits derived feature names as <source>_change_<lag>_<unit>. The declared inventory uses shorthand IDs. This map is the verified correspondence; a declared ID absent from this map has no implemented derivation in this checkout.

production_snapshot_observation.statement: Several declared variables without a local versioned archive were observed as exact top-level fields in stored production snapshot exports during earlier work. That evidence is retrospective: storage timestamps are proxies and no publication or vintage metadata accompanies the values.
production_snapshot_observation.coverage_claim: Earlier work reported nineteen of the twenty-eight declared variables present as exact top-level values and nine requiring missing, nested or alias review.
production_snapshot_observation.admissible_for: descriptive retrospective association only, with the storage-proxy label retained
not_admissible_for: counting as verified local source coverage

unresolved_policies: XAU/USD trading-session open, close, holiday and early-close calendar for the five-trading-day horizon.
Anchor-to-candle alignment rule for the one-hour and four-hour horizons when a release does not fall on an H1 boundary.
Whether partial or incomplete H1 bars are admissible, and how they are labelled.
Volatility estimator, sampling window and annualisation for trailing price volatility.
Revival or replacement decision for the ICE DXY, Fed-bias and regime variables that have no local source.
Whether repeated releases in one daily observation are treated as one observation or as separate overlapping events.
known_gaps: Nine declared variables and their transformations (dxy_level, dxy_d1, dxy_d5, dxy_d20, fed_bias, inflation_signal, risk_headline_context, equities_regime, growth_regime) have no verified local source.
Six declared transformations have no implemented derivation: dxy_d1, dxy_d5, dxy_d20, gold_d1_pct, gold_d5_pct and gold_d20_pct. Their names exist only as live-agent or asset-builder inputs.
Archived event consensus values are not authenticated pre-release vintages, so every event surprise remains retrospective evidence.
The immediate sub-hourly event window is unsupported at the available H1 resolution and must not be approximated from H1 bars.
No trading-session calendar is declared, so five-trading-day horizon and trailing five-day context coverage cannot yet be reported as passed or failed.
The originally supplied external research documents were unavailable, so originally claimed input sets beyond the repository logic document remain unverified.
